table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5)
table.description: Main idle speed target by coolant in normal running; this is the table to edit to change idle speed on a manual car. Automatic/CVT cars use Mode 6 instead.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding. With the manual coding the idle mode never becomes 6 (0x0F2BCC passes the mode through unchanged while FFF88ADA bit 7 is set, and 0x0F354C produces only modes 1-5 and 7, read), so on a manual car edit Mode 5. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 6 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant right after a start (below 75 degC coolant) until the car moves or the engine warms to 50 degC, and while the engine is stopped. Raise for a higher fast-idle after cold starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start), until the car moves. Raise for a higher idle right after hot starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant once the car has driven off after a cold start but the engine is still warming up (until coolant is above about 75 degC); then idle returns to Mode 5. Used on manual cars.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 7 is mapped to 8 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (read, 0x0F2BCC). Never on a manual car. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 8 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred).
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding, while the in-Drive idle condition FFF8A7E4 bit 0 is set (see Idle Air Reduction In Drive (Coolant): automatic coding, neutral input clear, pedal released, slow) and afterwards until the in-Drive idle air reduction FFF8B160 has ramped back to its target. Never on a manual car (inferred from that chain). 0x0F2248 (read): when FFF8A7E4 bit 4 is set, B242 = this(coolant) << 6 (12.5 rpm per count) replaces the idle-mode target chain. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Minimum (Baro, Oil Temp)
table.description: Floor on the idle speed target by barometric pressure and oil temperature; the ECU idles at no less than this.

table.name: Idle Post-Start Mode Exit Coolant
table.description: Coolant temperature, by coolant at start, at which idle leaves the post-start mode for normal warm idle (it also leaves once the car moves).

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 2)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 2 (cold post-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 3)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 3 (warm-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 2 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 2 to 7)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 3 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 3 to 7)

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 7 to 5)

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 1 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request (Alternate)
table.description:
Minimum idle speed requested by another module over CAN, by request code.
0x10EA40 (read; 20 ms task 0x1E0AE8 via 0x113060): while the network variant / frame gate holds (FFF88E0C bit 3 with FFF88621 = 1, bit 4 with FFF88618 = 1, or bit 7 with FFF88618 = 1) and FFF8A9A3 bit 0 is set, FFF8B3FA = this(CAN code FFF8A88A) for cal 0x35534 = 250 passes (5 s), then it falls by cal 0x35532 = 5 counts (1 rpm) per pass; 0 when FFF8A9A3 bit 0 clears. 0x10EB1C takes FFF854E2 = max(B3FA, a second request from FFF8A8D9 = CAN FFF88B90 + 26 scaled by cal 0x3555C, limited to cal 0x35556 = 1500 rpm), optionally remaps it through 05D3C0 / 05D3CC, and stores FFF8B3FC. FFF8B3FC's only reader is 0x0EE338, which passes it to the idle target module 0x0F2274 as stack argument 7 (disassembly at 0x0EF2E4, read); there min(B3FC, 0x1E00) >> 6 (12.5 rpm units) is maxed into a minimum idle-speed request only when param_1 = cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 and FFF8A9A2 bit 6 are both set (0x0F2826 reads @(158,R15) = param_11, read). Cal 0x1D0AE = 0, the same switch that keeps the alternate A/C idle air path and radiator-fan duty tables off. Unit: rpm x 5.12 (read from the >> 6 into 12.5 rpm units and the 0x1E00 = 1500 rpm cap). Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Alternate)
table.description:
Remaps the CAN idle speed request before it is applied.
0x10EB1C (read, disassembly 0x10EC56-0x10EC7A): the combined request FFF854E2 (input) is passed through this table into FFF8B3FC when FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is set and FFF8A8A1 bit 7 is clear; with both set 05D3CC is used instead; with FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear the request is stored unchanged; with FFF88B8E bit 0 (CAN 0x280) the output is cal 0x3555E (0). FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is always set on the manual coding (brief), so this is the table that would apply. Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Flag Set, Alternate)
table.description:
Alternative remap of the CAN idle speed request, used when an unidentified CAN flag is set.
0x10EB1C (read): used instead of 05D3C0 when FFF8A8A1 bit 7 is also set; FFF8A8A1 bit 7 comes from CAN bits FFF88B95 bits 0/1 via 0x11BBB4 (read, meaning not identified). Input = combined request FFF854E2. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Mode 5)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle (the warm-idle mode on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. At a settled warm idle the TGVs are normally commanded closed, so Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed) is probably the table in use: change both together, and together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) so idle feedback does not have to learn the difference.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) and Idle Base Air (Mode 5).

table.name: Idle Base Air (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant right after a cold start (below 75 degC) until the car moves or the engine warms, and while stopped, used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Post-Start, Modes 1/2, TGV Closed)

Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start) until the car moves, used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm Start, Mode 3, TGV Closed)

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

Never on a manual car (read, 0x0F2BCC). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6, TGV Closed)
table.description:

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial)
table.description: Extra idle air right after start, by start type (first start, restart, after a stall, remote start; start-type meanings inferred) and coolant. It is held after start, then decays by Post-Start Idle Air Decay once rpm reaches the idle target.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial, TGV Closed)
table.description: TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air (Initial): extra idle air right after start by start type and coolant, held and then decayed once rpm reaches the idle target.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms to the post-start idle air once rpm has reached the idle target and Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay has passed, by start type and coolant. Smaller = faster fade.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay (TGV Closed)
table.description: TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air Decay: multiplier applied every 40 ms to the post-start idle air after the decay delay. Smaller = faster fade.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay
table.description: Time after start, by start type and coolant at start, before the post-start idle air starts to decay (rpm must also have reached the idle target). Longer = extra air held longer.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Start Time
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air starts to rise, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air End Time
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air stops rising and starts to decay, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Level
table.description: Peak level of the staged post-start air, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Ramp Step
table.description: Rise of the staged post-start air every 40 ms between Start Time and End Time, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Decay
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms after End Time, by start type and coolant (smaller = faster fade). Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air IAT Add
table.description: Added to Post-Start Staged Air Level by intake air temperature, for the timed post-start air bump.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Steady (A/C Load Sw On, Neutral Sw Off, Above 14 km/h)
table.description: Extra idle air held while the A/C compressor is engaged, for: A/C load switch on, neutral switch off, car moving above 14 km/h. Raise if idle sags with the A/C on, lower if it flares. The A/C load switch meaning is inferred.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Initial Kick (A/C Load Sw On, Neutral Sw Off, Above 14 km/h)

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, Coolant)
table.description:
Idle air taken away, by coolant, while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive (pedal released, slow) to offset the load of the transmission. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only while FFF8A7E4 bit 0 is set (0x0F38D0, read): automatic coding (FFF886AB bit 7 clear) and the neutral input FFF88ADA bit 6 clear, accelerator released, speed FFF99835 within cals 0x2583F..0x25841, rpm below cal 0x25842 and below @025886(coolant), no speed-sensor/CAN faults; so never on a manual car (read). 0x0EAA40 (read): FFF8B162 = this(coolant) + Idle Air Reduction In Drive (RPM Error)(rpm - target rpm FFF8B236, coolant) + a ramp term (cals 0x25838..0x2583C), >= 0, capped by @025846(coolant); FFF8B160 follows it at cal 0x25834/0x25836 (86) per pass and is subtracted at half weight from the idle air FFF8B200 (0x0F0AF8, read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, RPM Error)
table.description:
Correction to Idle Air Reduction In Drive by rpm error (actual minus target) and coolant, for automatic/CVT cars idling in Drive. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: see Idle Air Reduction In Drive (Coolant) (automatic coding only). 0x0EAA40 (read): added to the coolant term with the rpm error FFF8CE9C - FFF8B236 (s16, rpm x 5.12) and coolant FFF88A44 as axes. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Minimum Idle Air (Moving in Gear)
table.description: Floor on idle air by rpm (and coolant) whenever the car is moving in gear, so the throttle cannot close below it; acts mainly as a dashpot when the pedal is released (inferred). Raise to soften throttle closing on decel; lower for faster rpm drop. Not used at standstill or in neutral.

table.name: Pull-Away Anti-Stall Air
table.description: Manual cars only: extra air, by how far rpm has dipped below a held reference, while pulling away from a standstill in gear with the pedal pressed. Raise to make launches from rest harder to stall.

table.name: Pull-Away Anti-Stall Reference Decay
table.description: Manual cars only: how fast (by rpm) the reference rpm used by Pull-Away Anti-Stall Air falls per combustion event, so dips are measured from the recent peak.

table.name: Pull-Away Anti-Stall Reference Offset
table.description: Manual cars only: offset (by rpm) subtracted from the predicted reference rpm for Pull-Away Anti-Stall Air; a positive value probably means a dip must be larger before the anti-stall air reacts.

table.name: Idle RPM-Drop Recovery Air (Drop Slowing)
table.description: Extra idle air, by rpm change rate, to catch an rpm dip at idle once the drop is easing (pedal released, rpm at least 40 below target).

table.name: Idle RPM-Drop Recovery Air (Drop Continuing)
table.description: Extra idle air, by how fast rpm is falling, to catch an rpm dip at idle (pedal released, rpm at least 40 below target, at least 5 s after start). Used while the drop is not easing; see the Drop Slowing table.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward (AT/CVT, State 0/5)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward, used in two transmission states only: extra or less idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step.
Details: 0x0ECA08 (read; call 0x0ECA88/0x0ECA94 R5 checked): while FFF88A26 bit0 (idle, inferred), engine running (FFF88A27 bit0 clear) and FFF99835 below cal 0x259C8 (255, i.e. always), B1AE = this(new target - ramped target = B236 - B23C/4, capped at cal 0x259CA = 1000 rpm); B1AE enters the idle air at half weight. A positive step (target raised) adds air ahead of the ramp. Used when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear (bit0 = FFF8A7DD in 1..4 or 6, 0x0F38B0). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward
table.description: Extra (or less) idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step, so rpm follows the new target without waiting for feedback. Positive steps add air. Used at idle on manual cars (and most automatic states).

table.name: Idle Air Trim (Charging Command)
table.description: Idle air trim by the alternator charging command. Probably compensates for lower alternator load.

table.name: Electrical Load Idle Air Hold Release (Alternator Command)
table.description: Flag table by alternator command that decides when the CAN load-value idle air adder (Idle Air Adder, CAN Load Value table) may increase while battery voltage is low.

table.name: Idle Air Adder (CAN 0x370 Load Value)
table.description: Extra idle air by a load value received over CAN, probably electrical load (not confirmed), added to the accessory idle air.

table.name: Idle Air Adder (CAN 0x280 Stage)
table.description: Extra idle air by a 3-bit stage value received over CAN, used only with one body coding. Possibly the radiator fan stage, but that is a guess.

table.name: Idle Air from Throttle Area (Torque Request)
table.description: Converts a throttle area back into idle air units when another module requests torque over CAN. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).

table.name: Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4 with the TGVs commanded closed.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Stop-Start Restart)
table.description:
Post-start idle air for an automatic stop-start restart, by start type and coolant. the stop-start feature appears unable to activate in this calibration.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read; args per call in module 0x0EE338): post-start idle air B20E = max(start air, staged air 05C49C family), added to the idle air at half weight (0x0F0AF8). TGVs not forced closed. Selected instead of the cranking value only inside the engine stop-start restart window (FFF89053 bit3/bit4 with the FFF88ADA bit3 edge, before the decay delay), by start type FFF8A6E8 (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Stop-Start Restart, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Post-start idle air for an automatic stop-start restart with the TGVs closed. the stop-start feature appears unable to activate in this calibration.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read; args per call in module 0x0EE338): post-start idle air B20E = max(start air, staged air 05C49C family), added to the idle air at half weight (0x0F0AF8). TGVs closed (FFF8A881 bit4). Selected instead of the cranking value only inside the engine stop-start restart window (FFF89053 bit3/bit4 with the FFF88ADA bit3 edge, before the decay delay), by start type FFF8A6E8 (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). Confidence: read.

table.name: A/C Idle Air (Alternate, Target RPM)
table.description:
A/C idle air by an unidentified CAN load value and idle target rpm, for an alternate A/C idle-air path.
Details: When used: with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set and cal 0x23CE9 bit 0 clear: A/C idle air FFF8B1A0 = max(this(FFF8A8C6, idle target FFF8B236), kick, cal 0x3539A = 712) while FFF8A9A3 bit 0 (0x0EC10C, read). 2376 base-air units, rising with FFF8A8C6. Alternate A/C idle-air path of 0x0EC10C (10 ms idle module 0x0EE338; call checked in the disassembly). Row input FFF8A8C6 = cal 0x3555C (121) x received byte FFF88B91 (CAN 0x280 byte 5) / 100, capped at cal 0x35A84 (128), or cal 0x35A85 when FFF88B8E bit 0 (0x115F80, read); filtered by cal 0x353C1 while A/C (A9A3 bit 0) is on. Its physical meaning is not identified (A/C load related, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: A/C Idle Air (Alternate, Engine Speed)
table.description:
A/C idle air by an unidentified CAN load value and engine speed, for an alternate A/C idle-air path.
Details: When used: with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set and cal 0x23CE9 bit 0 set: A/C idle air FFF8B1A0 = max(this(FFF8A8C6, engine speed FFF8CE9C filtered by cal 0x353C2 while A/C is on), kick, cal 0x3539A) (0x0EC10C; column input checked in the disassembly at 0x0EC200..0x0EC21A, read). Alternate A/C idle-air path of 0x0EC10C (10 ms idle module 0x0EE338; call checked in the disassembly). Row input FFF8A8C6 = cal 0x3555C (121) x received byte FFF88B91 (CAN 0x280 byte 5) / 100, capped at cal 0x35A84 (128), or cal 0x35A85 when FFF88B8E bit 0 (0x115F80, read); filtered by cal 0x353C1 while A/C (A9A3 bit 0) is on. Its physical meaning is not identified (A/C load related, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Initial Kick (Alternate)
table.description:
Initial A/C idle air kick by an unidentified CAN code, for an alternate A/C idle-air path.
Details: When used: with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set, while FFF8A9A3 bit 0 is set and the time since it was set is below A/C Idle Air Kick Duration: kick = this(FFF8A88A), afterwards the kick falls by cal 0x3539C (23) per 10 ms (0x0EC10C, read). FFF8A88A is a 0..6 code from received bits FFF88B8D 5-7 (CAN 0x280 byte 4 bits 5-7; 0x10E8C4 / 0x10E9C0, read; meaning not identified). Alternate A/C idle-air path of 0x0EC10C (10 ms idle module 0x0EE338; call checked in the disassembly). The sibling 2D tables' row input FFF8A8C6 (not used by this table) = cal 0x3555C (121) x received byte FFF88B91 (CAN 0x280 byte 5) / 100, capped at cal 0x35A84 (128), or cal 0x35A85 when FFF88B8E bit 0 (0x115F80, read); filtered by cal 0x353C1 while A/C (A9A3 bit 0) is on. Its physical meaning is not identified (A/C load related, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Kick Duration (Alternate)
table.description:
How long the alternate A/C idle air kick is held, by an unidentified CAN code.
Details: When used: with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set: the A/C idle-air kick (A/C Idle Air Initial Kick (Alternate)) is held while the 10 ms pass count since FFF8A9A3 bit 0 was set is below this(FFF8A88A) (0x0EC10C, read); FFF8A88A is a 0..6 code from received bits FFF88B8D 5-7 (CAN 0x280 byte 4; meaning not identified). Alternate A/C idle-air path of 0x0EC10C (10 ms idle module 0x0EE338; call checked in the disassembly). The sibling 2D tables' row input FFF8A8C6 (not used by this table) = cal 0x3555C (121) x received byte FFF88B91 (CAN 0x280 byte 5) / 100, capped at cal 0x35A84 (128), or cal 0x35A85 when FFF88B8E bit 0 (0x115F80, read); filtered by cal 0x353C1 while A/C (A9A3 bit 0) is on. Its physical meaning is not identified (A/C load related, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Low Voltage Idle Request Threshold (Alternator Command)
table.description:
Battery voltage threshold, by alternator command, for a low-voltage idle-up request. Unused in this ROM: its result is never read, so editing it has no effect.
Details: Unused in this ROM: 0x0F2274 (read; stack arguments checked against the push order at 0x0EF0FE..0x0EF110) compares module voltage FFF88A7E with this(alternator command FFF8B718) when cal 0x57584 bit 6 is set (else with cal 0x34EE0 = 12.0 V), while time since start FFF88A76 >= cal 0x34EE6 (10 s). Low for cal 0x34EE8 (15 s) gives cal 0x34EE2 (67), recovered after cal 0x34EE4 (300 s); the result goes only to FFF8A7F4, which nothing reads (ram_xref: one writer, no reader; its address appears only in the init 0x0ED850 and in this call). Editing it has no effect. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Feedback Map (Target MAP Offset)
table.description: Probably the main idle speed feedback map: how much the target manifold pressure (air) is raised or cut, by rpm error from the idle target and how fast rpm is changing. Positive = more air. Larger values give a stronger correction but risk hunting. Only active while idle feedback is on.

table.name: Idle Speed Feedback RPM Error Factor (Above Target)
table.description: Scales the rpm error used by the idle feedback when rpm is above the idle target. Lower values make the feedback react less to overshoot.

table.name: Idle Speed Feedback Gain Multiplier (Time in Feedback)
table.description: Multiplier on both idle feedback gains by how long idle feedback has been running with rpm near target.

table.name: Idle Speed Torque Feedback P
table.description: Torque correction (ft-lb) for idle speed by idle target and rpm error (positive = engine too slow), used when idle is held by torque control (inferred), within about 500 rpm of the idle target.

table.name: Idle Speed Torque Feedback D
table.description: Torque correction (ft-lb) for idle speed by idle target and how fast rpm changed over the last 20 ms; damps rpm swings when idle is held by torque control (inferred), within about 500 rpm of the idle target.

table.name: Idle Speed Torque Feedback Reference Torque
table.description: Reference torque by rpm that scales the idle torque feedback (P and D): a larger value gives a smaller correction. Must not be set to 0 ft-lb, which zeroes the feedback.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Decay (Positive)
table.description: How fast the idle feedback air kept when leaving idle is bled off, by rpm change rate; this acts like a dashpot (inferred). Larger = faster release.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Decay (Negative)
table.description: How fast a negative leftover of idle feedback air is released after leaving idle, by rpm change rate. Larger = cancels sooner.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Positive)
table.description: Limit on a positive idle-feedback carry-over, as a fraction by throttle opening above idle. The carried-over air keeps the air idle feedback had added when leaving idle and releases it gradually (dashpot-like, inferred).

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Negative)
table.description: Limit on a negative idle-feedback carry-over, as a fraction by throttle opening above idle. The carried-over air keeps the air idle feedback had added when leaving idle and releases it gradually (dashpot-like, inferred).

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as stopped in gear for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: AT/CVT codings, standstill in gear. Input FFF88A44 (coolant, read in the disassembly by the same R5). 0x0EC7A4 (read; called from 0x0EE338 with FFF886AB bit 7, neutral FFF88ADA bit 6, CAN fault FFF88E2B bit 1, FFF8A7E2 bit 1, FFF8B140, coolant FFF88A44, time since start FFF88A76, speed FFF99835): on the manual coding FFF8A7DD is always 1, so these tables are AT/CVT only. FFF8B140 = engine rpm FFF8CD54 - FFF888AC x 128/25 (0x0E9EE8, read); FFF888AC comes from the TCM frame 0x148 (signals_rates_can.md, read), so B140 is the torque-converter slip in rpm (inferred). State 4 (stopped in gear) needs slip >= Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear) (hysteresis cal 0x25648), state 6 (neutral/park) needs slip > Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral) (hysteresis cal 0x25646) and FFF88A76 > cal 0x25642 (read). FFF8A7DD selects the idle table sets named "(AT/CVT, State...)" through FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (0x0F38B0). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as in neutral/park for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: AT/CVT codings, in neutral/park. Input FFF88A44 (coolant). 0x0EC7A4 (read; called from 0x0EE338 with FFF886AB bit 7, neutral FFF88ADA bit 6, CAN fault FFF88E2B bit 1, FFF8A7E2 bit 1, FFF8B140, coolant FFF88A44, time since start FFF88A76, speed FFF99835): on the manual coding FFF8A7DD is always 1, so these tables are AT/CVT only. FFF8B140 = engine rpm FFF8CD54 - FFF888AC x 128/25 (0x0E9EE8, read); FFF888AC comes from the TCM frame 0x148 (signals_rates_can.md, read), so B140 is the torque-converter slip in rpm (inferred). State 4 (stopped in gear) needs slip >= Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear) (hysteresis cal 0x25648), state 6 (neutral/park) needs slip > Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral) (hysteresis cal 0x25646) and FFF88A76 > cal 0x25642 (read). FFF8A7DD selects the idle table sets named "(AT/CVT, State...)" through FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (0x0F38B0). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (Before First Transfer)
table.description: Long-term idle learning speed used after an idle-learn reset until the first learned value has been stored.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (A/C Off)
table.description: How fast the long-term idle air learning follows the current correction with the A/C off, by time since the last learning transfer. Larger = learns faster but less stable.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (A/C On)
table.description: How fast the long-term idle air learning follows the current correction with the A/C on, by time since the last learning transfer. Larger = learns faster but less stable.

table.name: Idle Learn Bias Index Step
table.description: How the drive-history index for Idle Learn Bias moves every 2 s, by vehicle speed (only with coolant at or above 80 degC).

table.name: Idle Learn Bias
table.description: Offset added to the long-term idle air learning by a drive-history index: long idling pushes the learned idle air down, sustained driving pushes it up (purpose, e.g. heat soak, inferred). Index movement is set by Idle Learn Bias Index Step.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Open)
table.description: Main EGR rate target (% of intake charge, probably external EGR) by rpm and load while the TGVs are open. 0 = no EGR. Capped by EGR Target Rate Maximum.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Closed)
table.description: Main EGR rate target (% of intake charge, probably external EGR) by rpm and load while the TGVs are closed. 0 = no EGR. Raising it adds more exhaust gas at light load. Capped by EGR Target Rate Maximum.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Maximum
table.description: Hard cap on the target EGR rate.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (255 = 1.0) by coolant on the target EGR rate.

table.name: EGR Target Rate DAM Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the target EGR rate by the knock learning value (probably DAM).

table.name: EGR Target Rate Reduction Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (255 = 1.0) by rpm and load that reduces the target EGR rate while an unidentified module requests it and EGR flow is present. When the request is active is not known.

table.name: EGR Enable Minimum Air after Start
table.description: Amount of air (probably the air drawn since start), by coolant at start, that must pass before EGR is enabled.

table.name: EGR Enable Coolant Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when coolant is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable Coolant Maximum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when coolant is at or below this.

table.name: EGR Enable RPM Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when rpm is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable RPM Maximum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when rpm is at or below this.

table.name: EGR Enable Load Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when load is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable Load Maximum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when load is at or below this.

table.name: EGR Enable Intake Air Temp Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when intake air temperature is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable Battery Voltage Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when battery voltage is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable Vehicle Speed Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when the car is moving at least this fast (vehicle speed signal inferred).

table.name: EGR Enable Exhaust Pressure Margin
table.description: EGR is only enabled when the estimated pressure upstream of the EGR valve exceeds manifold pressure by at least this much, so exhaust gas can actually flow.

table.name: EGR Active Threshold
table.description: Target EGR rate above which EGR counts as active, which switches ignition to the Base Timing (EGR Active) tables. See EGR Active Threshold Hysteresis for the switch-off point.

table.name: EGR Active Threshold Hysteresis
table.description: How far below EGR Active Threshold the target EGR rate must fall before EGR counts as inactive again.

table.name: EGR Timing Advance (TGV Closed)
table.description: Extra timing advance requested while EGR is active with the TGVs closed, by rpm and load, scaled by how much EGR is flowing. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, so it reaches the spark only where that request (plus knock advance) is below the Base Timing (EGR Active) map, never above it.

table.name: EGR Timing Advance (TGV Open)
table.description: Extra timing advance requested while EGR is active with the TGVs open, by rpm and load, scaled by how much EGR is flowing. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, so it reaches the spark only where that request (plus knock advance) is below the Base Timing (EGR Active) map, never above it.

table.name: EGR Coolant Timing Adjustment (TGV Closed)
table.description: Timing adjustment by rpm and load while EGR is active and the TGVs are closed, scaled by EGR Coolant Timing Adjustment Coolant Multiplier so it acts only on a cooler engine. It is added to both base timing and the timing request, so it moves the fired timing directly.

table.name: EGR Coolant Timing Adjustment Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (255 = 1.0) by coolant on the EGR timing adjustment tables.

table.name: EGR Target Flow Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by coolant and load on the target EGR flow that drives the valve.

table.name: EGR Valve Position from Target Flow
table.description: Feed-forward EGR valve position (steps) for a target EGR flow; feedback is added on top.

table.name: EGR Valve Flow Model
table.description: Estimated EGR flow by pressure difference across the valve and valve position. Used both for the actual EGR flow estimate and for the flow feedback, so edits change both.

table.name: EGR Valve Flow Feedback Integral Step
table.description: How fast the EGR valve feedback corrects position, by the error between target and modelled flow. Positive opens the valve. Larger = faster correction, more risk of hunting.

table.name: EGR Valve Feedback Integral Minimum
table.description: Lower limit of the EGR valve flow-feedback correction (how far feedback may close the valve below feed-forward).

table.name: EGR Valve Feedback Integral Maximum
table.description: Upper limit of the EGR valve flow-feedback correction (how far feedback may open the valve beyond feed-forward).

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Estimate
table.description: Estimated pressure upstream of the EGR valve (probably exhaust side) by rpm and load. The difference to manifold pressure sets the modelled EGR flow and decides whether EGR may be enabled.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Open, Multi-Injection)
table.description:
EGR rate target by rpm and load with the TGVs open and multiple injections per cycle.
Details: When used: TGVs not closed and multi-injection active (FFF8A775 bit 1); cal 0x2F797 bit 5 clear. Base target EGR rate A818, looked up by 0x0FA10C with rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616 (read, disassembly). Target EGR rate (0x0FA260, read): FFF8A81A = base A817 x Coolant Multiplier 05CB04/255 x 255/255 (A816) x Reduction Multiplier A81C/255 x DAM Multiplier 05CB10/128, x 640 (1/640 units), capped at cal 0x2C4E6 (192 = 30 %) and forced to 0 unless the enable conditions FFF8A811 bit 0 hold (0x0FAAFC). A817 follows the base table A818 (0x0FA068). Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). 0 = no EGR. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Closed, Multi-Injection)
table.description:
EGR rate target by rpm and load with the TGVs closed and multiple injections per cycle.
Details: When used: TGVs closed and multi-injection active (FFF8A775 bit 1); cal 0x2F797 bit 5 clear. Base target EGR rate A818, looked up by 0x0FA10C with rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616 (read, disassembly). Target EGR rate (0x0FA260, read): FFF8A81A = base A817 x Coolant Multiplier 05CB04/255 x 255/255 (A816) x Reduction Multiplier A81C/255 x DAM Multiplier 05CB10/128, x 640 (1/640 units), capped at cal 0x2C4E6 (192 = 30 %) and forced to 0 unless the enable conditions FFF8A811 bit 0 hold (0x0FAAFC). A817 follows the base table A818 (0x0FA068). Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). table.name: EGR Target Rate (Alternate, TGV Open)
table.description:

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Open)
table.description:
Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs open.

The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). table.name: EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration
table.description:
How long, by manifold pressure, the EGR tip-out cap is held after a pedal tip-out.
0x0FA068 (read): looked up with FFF8869C (copy of MAP FFF88A34, read) on the rising edge of the tip-out flag; while the flag counter FFF8B2A8 is below it, the target is held at the tip-out limit. p16 (read): EGR module 0x0F94A8 runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Timing Advance (Multi-Injection, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Multi-injection copy of EGR Timing Advance (TGV Closed).
Details: When used: only while FFF8A775 bit 2 is set. TGV-closed side. 0x0DC97C / 0x0DD0DC (read): v = TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8, each table read as x/2 - 64 degrees;; stored as 2 x deg + 128 in FFF8A763 (single injection) / FFF8A767. FFF8A769 = FFF8A767 when FFF8A775 bit 2 is set (all four injectors in a 2- or 3-injection strategy, 0x0FAABC), else FFF8A763 (0x0DD454, read). FFF8A769 enters the timing request FFF8A78A (0x0E0A30) and the alternate final-timing value FFF8A733 of 0x0D9E40 (read). Through the request it reaches the fired timing wherever Primary Ignition + this + KCA + FLKC is below the Base Timing (EGR Active) map: 0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568 give fired base = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed). It can never lift the fired timing above the Base Timing (EGR Active) maps. Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (400-6400 rpm, 10-240 %; rows above 32768 are padding). Confidence: read.
