table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Modes 1/4, Default/Sport Sharp)
table.description: Main requested-torque threshold, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close (drive modes 1 and 4, the default); they reopen above the matching Exit table. Coolant and air-flow conditions also apply.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Drive Modes 1/4, Default/Sport Sharp)
table.description: Main requested-torque threshold, by rpm, above which a TGV-close request clears (drive modes 1 and 4, the default). Keep above the Enter table.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close in drive mode 2. The TGVs probably close at light load: requested torque must fall below the Enter table to close them and rise above the matching Exit table to reopen (with coolant and air-flow conditions).

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, above which a TGV-close request clears in drive mode 2. Keep above TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Mode 2, Sport). The TGVs probably close at light load: requested torque must fall below the Enter table to close them and rise above the matching Exit table to reopen (with coolant and air-flow conditions).

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close in drive mode 3. The TGVs probably close at light load: requested torque must fall below the Enter table to close them and rise above the matching Exit table to reopen (with coolant and air-flow conditions).

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, above which a TGV-close request clears in drive mode 3. Keep above TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent). The TGVs probably close at light load: requested torque must fall below the Enter table to close them and rise above the matching Exit table to reopen (with coolant and air-flow conditions).

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Offset
table.description: Offset added to every TGV torque threshold (except the start-mode pair) by rpm and an unidentified signal; 0 ft-lb means no change.

table.name: TGV IAT Threshold
table.description: Intake air temperature, by vehicle speed, below which the TGVs are kept open even when the torque, coolant and air-flow close conditions hold (the close request is replaced by a 'blocked' state that resets the close timer). Raise it to keep the TGVs open in cold air at speed.

table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum
table.description: Minimum coolant temperature for the TGVs to close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions).

table.name: TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter)
table.description: Air flow below which the TGVs may close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions together with torque and coolant). Raise it (with TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Exit)) to let the TGVs close at higher air flow; once closed they reopen above the Exit value.

table.name: TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Exit)
table.description: Air flow above which a TGV-close request clears again (probably reopening the TGVs); the upper end of the hysteresis with TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter). Keep it above the Enter value.

table.name: TGV Close Delay
table.description: How long the TGV-close conditions must hold before the TGVs actually close, by vehicle speed. Longer = fewer TGV switches during brief light-load moments.

table.name: TGV Open Fraction from Position (Closing)
table.description: Converts measured TGV position into the open fraction used to blend every TGV-open / TGV-closed table (fuel, timing, AVCS) while the TGVs are closing; the blend also cannot fall faster than about 0.5 s from open to closed.

table.name: TGV Open Fraction from Position (Opening)
table.description: Converts measured TGV position into the open fraction used to blend every TGV-open / TGV-closed table (fuel, timing, AVCS) while the TGVs are opening; the blend ramps at about 1 s from closed to open unless the valves open faster.

table.name: TGV Motor Duty Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the TGV motor drive duty by coolant and battery voltage, so the valves move reliably when cold or at low voltage.

table.name: TGV Drive Duty (Opening)
table.description: Motor duty used to drive the TGVs towards their open stop, by valve position (open meaning inferred). Leave alone unless the TGV actuators are changed.

table.name: TGV Drive Duty (Closing)
table.description: Motor duty used to drive the TGVs towards their closed stop, by valve position (closed meaning inferred). Leave alone unless the TGV actuators are changed.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Start Modes)
table.description:
Requested-torque threshold for TGV closing in a start combustion mode.
TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). used without the offset only while FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B4A. Confidence: read.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Start Modes)
table.description:
Exit threshold paired with TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Start Modes).
TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Pairs with TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Start Modes). Confidence: read.

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Other Drive Modes)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Used in the default drive mode (cruise meaning inferred). If you change Requested Torque tables, cruise response changes unless this is adjusted too.

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Used in drive mode 2 (cruise meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Used in drive mode 3 (cruise meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Other Drive Modes, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Default drive mode with the meter cruise option (cruise meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Drive Mode 2, Sport, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Used in drive mode 2 with the meter cruise option (cruise meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Used in drive mode 3 with the meter cruise option (cruise meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. This is the standard km/h version.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. Standard mph version.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. km/h version with the meter cruise option.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. mph-meter version with the meter cruise option.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter, Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. km/h version with the meter cruise option and an untraced alternate flag.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter, Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. mph version with the meter cruise option and an untraced alternate flag.

table.name: Cruise Cancel Speed
table.description: Speed below which cruise control cancels (and the set speed is cleared), by meter (market) code.

table.name: Cruise Set Speed Ramp While Accelerating
table.description: How fast the cruise target speed rises, by speed, while the raise (accelerate) switch is held.

table.name: Cruise Torque Limit Offset
table.description: Torque margin by rpm that caps the cruise control torque request above a base torque value, limiting how hard cruise can drive the engine. One table edits all three copies (including the monitor copy).

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Default)
table.description: Main cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error, used while holding speed and in all states without their own table. Higher = more aggressive throttle response.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0x23)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after a short tap of the raise (accelerate) switch (tap meaning inferred). Higher = more aggressive throttle response.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0xB0)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after a short tap of the lowering (coast) switch (tap meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Catch-Up)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error, used while the car catches up to a set speed changed by holding a switch (inferred). Higher = more aggressive throttle response.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0x40)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after the raise switch, while not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed. Higher = more aggressive throttle response.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Set-Speed Approach)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error while approaching a new set speed, until within about 3 km/h of it.

table.name: Cruise Integrator Preset (Engage)
table.description: Value the cruise controller's integral term is preset to when cruise starts controlling or returns to holding speed, by speed and acceleration.

table.name: Cruise Integrator Preset (After Tap)
table.description: Value the cruise controller's integral term is preset to after a set-speed switch tap, by speed and acceleration, so speed settles smoothly.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed from CAN Speed
table.description: Converts the CAN vehicle speed into the speed used by cruise control, per meter (market) code, as a straight line (scale and offset). The offsets probably make the set speed match the speedometer.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed Filter Weight
table.description: Smoothing weight for the vehicle speed used by cruise control, by speed error and speed. Larger = less smoothing, quicker reaction.

table.name: Cruise Excess Acceleration Threshold (Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: With one cruise option and an alternate flag only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 0.2 s while cruise is on without pedal input, cruise ends (probably a runaway check).

table.name: Cruise Acceleration Cancel Threshold (Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: With one cruise option only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 3 s while cruise is on, cruise is cancelled and stays unavailable for the rest of the drive (probably a runaway check).

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0xC0)
table.description: Cruise controller gain used in a cruise state probably linked to the lowering switch (inferred), when Cruise Speed Error Gain (Set-Speed Approach) is not active.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Ramp-Down Rate
table.description: How fast, by vehicle speed, brake override ramps the accelerator signal down. Larger = faster torque cut when brake and accelerator overlap. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Floor
table.description: Lowest pedal value, by vehicle speed, that brake override ramps the accelerator signal down to. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Rate (Pedal Held)
table.description: How fast, by vehicle speed, the pedal limit is raised again after the brake is released while the driver keeps the accelerator pressed. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Time
table.description: Time, by vehicle speed, over which full pedal is restored after brake override ends (recovery ends early if the pedal is released or reached). Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Brake Pressure Threshold
table.description: Brake pressure, by booster vacuum and vehicle speed, above which the brake counts as applied for brake override. Raise to make override need a firmer brake press. Used while the brake-pressure signal from the stability control unit is valid. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Delay
table.description: How long the brake must be pressed over a held accelerator, by pedal position and speed, before brake override starts cutting the pedal signal (above 7 km/h). Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Deceleration Threshold (No Pressure Signal)

scaling.units: ms per km/h of speed drop
ms per mph of speed drop

table.description: Deceleration needed (by pedal and speed) to confirm braking when the brake-pressure signal is not available, so brake override can still act from the brake switch. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: VDC Torque Request Correction
table.description: Correction, by the gap between the stability control (VDC) torque request and actual engine torque, that sets how tightly the ECU limits target torque during a VDC torque reduction (VDC meaning inferred).

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Maximum
table.description:
Upper limit, by barometric pressure, of a modelled brake-booster vacuum.
Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x182B28 (read, all stack args checked in the assembly) has three sources for the booster vacuum FFF8BAFC: cal 0x57585 bit 5 set = baro - analog pressure input FFF88D10; else bit 6 = fixed cal 0x43402 (50 kPa); else a model from manifold vacuum baro FFF88668 - MAP FFF88A34: while not braking at low manifold vacuum (FFF8AC90 bit 3 clear) the estimate is filtered (cal 0x43406) up towards the manifold vacuum as long as it is below this(baro); during braking it is reduced by 253 x 13/100 per count of brake-pressure rise (FFF8AC93 - FFF8AC92). Confidence: read.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Manifold Threshold
table.description:
Manifold-vacuum threshold, by barometric pressure, for a brake-booster vacuum model.
Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x18390C (read): FFF8AC90 bit 3 = brake pressure FFF8AC94 >= cal 0x435BD (1) and FFF88A38 >= this(baro FFF88668) - 12800 (FFF88A38 = (MAP - baro)/2, so MAP - baro >= (this - 12800)/128 kPa), i.e. braking with too little manifold vacuum to recharge the booster. Bit 3 feeds only the brake-pressure latches FFF8AC92 / FFF8AC93 / FFF8BAFE and the manifold-vacuum model of 0x182B28, whose results are unused while cal 0x57585 bit 5 is set and FFF8BB00 has no reader (read, grep). Confidence: read.

table.name: Alternator Command from Target Voltage
table.description: Alternator control duty by target charging voltage (probably). Changing it changes the charging voltage the alternator actually reaches. Also feeds Idle Air Trim (Charging Command).

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant)
table.description:
Radiator fan duty by coolant for an alternate (duty-based) fan control path.
With cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set, 0x0F8AAC (read) uses this when received byte FFF88BAA (CAN 0x282 byte 3) < cal 0x342EC (148, 146 to fall back) and FFF8A807 bit 5 is clear: duty B27C = this(coolant FFF88A44) once coolant >= cal 0x342DC (95 C, falls off 3 C lower), 100 % from cal 0x342E4 (100 C); used in fan mode 1 (0x0F7A88). Radiator fan module 0x0F7618 (40 ms task, read): the fan stage FFF8A805 (0/1/2) drives timer E channel 10 fully on for stage >= 1 (FFF9981C bit 0, 0x0F8F08 -> 0x1E417C -> 0x1D9B8E) and port PF6 for stage 2 (FFF9981C bit 4, 0x0F8E70 -> 0x1D4E56 -> PFDR), and feeds the idle air (0x0ECE60, 0x0F5248) and torque adders (0x0C2B2C); the stages follow coolant and the A/C request (0x0F8764), so a two-relay radiator fan (inferred). With the bit set, A805 = stage from the duty FFF8B278 (0x0F7EC4: stage 1 from 40 %, stage 2 from 70 %). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, Flag A807 Set)
table.description:
Radiator fan duty by coolant, used when an unidentified driving-condition flag is set.
With cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set, 0x0F8AAC (read) uses this when FFF88BAA < 148 and FFF8A807 bit 5 is set (0x0F8F98: a condition built from the A/C state, vehicle speed, rpm, load, IAT and SI-Drive mode; not identified); on threshold cal 0x3439C (98 C), full at cal 0x343A0 (101 C). Radiator fan module 0x0F7618 (40 ms task, read): the fan stage FFF8A805 (0/1/2) drives timer E channel 10 fully on for stage >= 1 (FFF9981C bit 0, 0x0F8F08 -> 0x1E417C -> 0x1D9B8E) and port PF6 for stage 2 (FFF9981C bit 4, 0x0F8E70 -> 0x1D4E56 -> PFDR), and feeds the idle air (0x0ECE60, 0x0F5248) and torque adders (0x0C2B2C); the stages follow coolant and the A/C request (0x0F8764), so a two-relay radiator fan (inferred). With the bit set, A805 = stage from the duty FFF8B278 (0x0F7EC4: stage 1 from 40 %, stage 2 from 70 %). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, CAN 0x282 Value High)
table.description:
Radiator fan duty by coolant, used when an unidentified CAN value is high.
With cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set, 0x0F8AAC (read) uses this when received byte FFF88BAA (CAN 0x282 byte 3, not identified) >= cal 0x342EC (148); on threshold cal 0x342D4 (95 C), full at cal 0x342D8 (100 C). Radiator fan module 0x0F7618 (40 ms task, read): the fan stage FFF8A805 (0/1/2) drives timer E channel 10 fully on for stage >= 1 (FFF9981C bit 0, 0x0F8F08 -> 0x1E417C -> 0x1D9B8E) and port PF6 for stage 2 (FFF9981C bit 4, 0x0F8E70 -> 0x1D4E56 -> PFDR), and feeds the idle air (0x0ECE60, 0x0F5248) and torque adders (0x0C2B2C); the stages follow coolant and the A/C request (0x0F8764), so a two-relay radiator fan (inferred). With the bit set, A805 = stage from the duty FFF8B278 (0x0F7EC4: stage 1 from 40 %, stage 2 from 70 %). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (A/C, CAN 0x280 Value)
table.description:
Radiator fan duty with the A/C requested, by an unidentified CAN value.
With cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set, 0x0F70B4 (read) sets B270 = 0 below FFF88B8F 68 (54 to switch off), 100 % from 252, else this(FFF88B8F); FFF88B8F is a received byte (CAN 0x280 byte 3, 0x085D20; physical meaning not identified). B270 is used in fan mode 7 (A/C requested, 0x0F8764): duty = max(cal 0x342D0 = 50 %, B270, coolant duty) (0x0F7A88, read). Radiator fan module 0x0F7618 (40 ms task, read): the fan stage FFF8A805 (0/1/2) drives timer E channel 10 fully on for stage >= 1 (FFF9981C bit 0, 0x0F8F08 -> 0x1E417C -> 0x1D9B8E) and port PF6 for stage 2 (FFF9981C bit 4, 0x0F8E70 -> 0x1D4E56 -> PFDR), and feeds the idle air (0x0ECE60, 0x0F5248) and torque adders (0x0C2B2C); the stages follow coolant and the A/C request (0x0F8764), so a two-relay radiator fan (inferred). With the bit set, A805 = stage from the duty FFF8B278 (0x0F7EC4: stage 1 from 40 %, stage 2 from 70 %). Confidence: read.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)
table.description: Engine torque by rpm and load at DAM 1.0, blended with the DAM 0 table by DAM. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. Mostly equal to Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Open); keep consistent if you change the torque model.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 0)
table.description: Engine torque by rpm and load at DAM 0, blended with the DAM 1.0 table by DAM. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. Close to, but somewhat lower than, the Engine Torque from Load (DAM 0) tables.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque)
table.description: Full-load air flow by rpm at Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque); a floor on the air used for the maximum-available torque the ECU sends over CAN (inferred). Raise it with a bigger turbo, or other modules see too low a torque capacity. Does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque)
table.description: Manifold pressure that Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) refers to, by rpm. Raising the boost limit raises the estimate in proportion, up to 1.25x. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow IAT Factor (CAN Torque)
table.description: Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by intake temperature ratio. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow Boost Limit Factor (CAN Torque)
table.description: Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by the ratio of the current boost limit to Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque). Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.

table.name: CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate
table.description: How fast, by rpm, the engine torque reported over CAN to other modules (for example stability control) fades out at a fuel cut and returns after it. It does not change fuelling or throttle.

table.name: MAF Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts MAF sensor voltage to airflow (g/s) in 64 fixed steps from 0 to 4.92 V; this airflow drives the ECU's air model, load and fuel. Rescale every point when fitting a bigger intake or a different MAF, and keep peak flow below the P0103 voltage limit. An internal 218 g/s cap on one copy of the airflow affects only purge, TGV, monitors and similar side functions, not fuel, load or timing.

table.name: MAP Sensor Multiplier
table.description: Gain of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt. For a 3-bar or larger sensor set it to the new sensor's slope and set MAP Sensor Offset to match. The ECU's MAP value cannot go above 256 kPa absolute (about 22 psi boost at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted, so anything higher reads as 256 kPa.

table.name: MAP Sensor Offset
table.description: Offset of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, i.e. the sensor's reading extrapolated to 0 V. Set it together with MAP Sensor Multiplier when fitting a different MAP sensor. The result is still limited to 256 kPa absolute.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage Floor
table.description: Lowest value the corrected MAF voltage may reach after the ECU subtracts its post-start MAF correction (a decaying start-up offset); it applies at all times after the first pass. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description: Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description: Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description: Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain.

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0107)
table.description: Sensor voltage below which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted low (P0107) and a substitute MAP is used. It works on raw voltage, so it does not change when you rescale the MAP sensor.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0108)
table.description: Sensor voltage above which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted high (P0108). Raw voltage, independent of the MAP scaling.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0102)
table.description: MAF voltage below which the MAF circuit-low code P0102 is set.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0103)
table.description: MAF voltage above which the MAF circuit-high code P0103 is set.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0112)
table.description: Voltage below which the main IAT sensor is flagged as shorted (reads impossibly hot, P0112).

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0113)
table.description: Voltage above which the main IAT sensor is flagged as open (reads impossibly cold, P0113).

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage Low Limit (P0097)
table.description: Voltage below which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0097).

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage High Limit (P0098)
table.description: Voltage above which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0098).

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0117)
table.description: Voltage below which the coolant sensor is flagged as shorted (P0117).

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0118)
table.description: Voltage above which the coolant sensor is flagged as open (P0118).

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0197)
table.description: Voltage below which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0197).

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0198)
table.description: Voltage above which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0198).

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0192)
table.description: Rail pressure sensor voltage below which P0192 (circuit low) is set.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0193)
table.description: Rail pressure sensor voltage above which P0193 (circuit high) is set.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Zero-Pressure Voltage
table.description: Rail pressure sensor voltage that reads as zero pressure. Change it with Rail Pressure Sensor Gain only when fitting a different rail pressure sensor.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Gain
table.description: Slope of the rail pressure sensor conversion. Change it only for a different rail pressure sensor.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Maximum
table.description: Highest rail pressure the sensor conversion can report.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Fault Value
table.description: Rail pressure the ECU assumes while the rail pressure sensor is faulted. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Multiplier
table.description: Gain of the ECU's barometric pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt. This sensor is probably inside the ECU; leave alone.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Offset
table.description: Offset of the barometric pressure sensor conversion. Leave alone.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Enable
table.description: When set, the ECU uses its barometric pressure sensor. When cleared, it assumes sea-level pressure (101.3 kPa) everywhere, so altitude compensation stops working. Bit 7 (value 128).

table.name: P0088 Rail Pressure High Limit
table.description: Fuel rail pressure limit for P0088 (rail pressure too high): the code trips when actual pressure exceeds this value plus a 2.5 MPa hysteresis for about 2 seconds, and also triggers fail-safe; after a trip, pressure must drop back to this value to recover. If you raise target rail pressure, keep peak actual pressure below this plus 2.5 MPa.

table.name: P0087 Rail Pressure Deviation Limit
table.description: How far actual rail pressure may fall below target (in normal high-pressure pump operation) before P0087 sets, after about 10 seconds. Raising it makes the code harder to set.

table.name: P0088 Rail Pressure Deviation Limit
table.description: How far actual rail pressure may rise above target (in normal high-pressure pump operation) before P0088 sets, after about 10 seconds. Raising it makes the code harder to set.

table.name: P0087 Rail Pressure Low Limit
table.description: Rail pressure floor by rpm for P0087 (rail pressure too low): the code counts a fault when actual pressure stays more than 0.30 MPa (hysteresis cal) below this value for about 10 seconds, and recovers when pressure is back at this value.

table.name: Cold Start Timing Monitor Band (Coolant)
table.description: Diagnostic threshold, not a tuning table: how far final timing may exceed the cold-start spark target, by coolant, before the P050B cold-start timing monitor counts a fault. One entry edits all three copies.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1
table.description: First reference for the P219A (A/F imbalance) monitor: how much the front A/F sensor reading may swing, by rpm and load, over the 25-second test window. Raising it makes P219A harder to set. A fault also needs A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1 to be exceeded. Above about 4000 rpm the reference climbs steeply (interpolating to the 4500 rpm row, which is effectively infinite), so running above about 4000 rpm during the window stops the test from failing.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2
table.description: Second, higher reference for the P219A (A/F imbalance) monitor, used with A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2 as confirmation. Raising it makes P219A harder to set. Above about 4000 rpm the reference climbs steeply (interpolating to the 4500 rpm row, which is effectively infinite), so running above about 4000 rpm during the window stops the test from failing.

table.name: EGR Enable
table.description: Master switch for EGR. Clearing it is expected to keep EGR off, so the EGR-off variants of base timing, closed loop target and throttle tables become the live ones (inferred). Bit 5 (value 32).

table.name: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT
table.description: Tells the ECU whether it is in a manual or an AT/CVT car (clear = manual in every manual image). It decides gear calculation, the gear torque limits and whether the AT/CVT Coding table variants are used. Do not change on a manual car. Bit 1 (value 2).

table.name: Transmission Coding: From Input Port
table.description: When set, the manual/automatic coding is read from a hardware input instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT. Bit 6 (value 64).

table.name: Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B
table.description: Enables the second (Path B) tip-in torque shaping. Leave clear unless you calibrate the whole Path B set. Bit 6 (value 64).

table.name: Open Loop Fueling: Use Alternate Map
table.description: When set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate) probably replaces the normal open loop fueling strategy. Bit 4 (value 16).

table.name: VE: Use AVCS-Not-Ready Table
table.description: When set, Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready) is used while the cams are probably not yet under control. Bit 0 (value 1).

table.name: Base Timing: Pedal-Released Tables Enable
table.description: Clear it to use the normal base timing tables off-throttle too. Bit 0 (value 1).

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 1
table.description: Allows double/triple injection while one of the high-pedal latches is set. Bit 0 (value 1).

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 2
table.description: Allows double/triple injection while a second high-pedal latch is set. Bit 1 (value 2).

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 3
table.description: Allows double/triple injection while a third high-pedal latch is set. Bit 2 (value 4).

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. Descriptor 05EB84. Confidence: read.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs open with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs open with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description: Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Knock-dependent extra enrichment for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its DAM multiplier (full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Fuel removed from the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its own DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). Leaning only works where Primary Open Loop Fueling is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. Descriptor 05AC80. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group plus its knock additive, used only with the 'Use Alternate Map' calibration switch set.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x2F79A bit 4 set and DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x1391C (16). Replaces the TGV/AVCS blend plus knock additive in FFF8A681. 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear. With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). Descriptor 05AC00. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). Descriptor 05A804. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description:
Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.
Details: When used: see Additional Enrichment A: B applies when coolant < cal 0x13E1A or rpm >= cal 0x13E0C (A when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E; in between the last value is held), and the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1. Second source table of FFF8AFE8. Descriptor 05A818. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Cold-Start Trim (TGVs Closed)
table.description: Small trim to the closed-loop target after a cold start, by start coolant and air used since start, with the TGVs closed.

table.name: Closed Loop Target (Catalyst Monitor Active)
table.description: Closed-loop target used instead of the four Closed Loop Target tables while the P0420 catalyst monitor test runs; not limited or trimmed by the other target tables.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 1 (TGV Open)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 1 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Open)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 1: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 1: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 2 (TGV Open)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 2 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 2 (TGV Open)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 2: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 2 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 2: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 3 (TGV Open)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 3 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 3 (TGV Open)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 3: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 3 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 3: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: Injection Timing (Double Injection, 1st)
table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. Descriptor 05AF94. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Injection Timing (Double Injection, 2nd)
table.description:
Angle of the second pulse with two injections per cycle.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the second pulse with two injections per cycle (0x0CB604, read). Injection angle for FFF8B056 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. Descriptor 05AFA8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Double Injection Split
table.description:
Share of the fuel in the first of two injections; the second gets the rest.
Details: Share of the fuel in the first of two injections (0x0D05D8 -> FFF8B068 -> FFF8A6D1, read); the second gets the rest (0x0D0D50). Limited by FFF8A6DA (read). Descriptor 05B1A0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed)
table.description: Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Closed)
table.description: First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Rpm x load correction to the phase 2 first-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Correction by spark target and coolant to the phase 2 first-pulse angle, TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Correction to the phase 2 second-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share (Idle, Alternate)
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection).

table.name: Purge Valve Duty
table.description: Purge valve duty needed for a target purge flow at a given manifold vacuum; higher vacuum needs less duty. Applied above Purge Valve Minimum Duty. Change only for a different purge valve.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Descriptor 05D044. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt, TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt) used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt, TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt) used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description: Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter used while the TGVs are closed. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used instead of the other Map A tables while the car is at a standstill under high load (speed 5 km/h or less, pedal 80 % or more, load 40 % or more, for 1 s). Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while an unidentified speed/pedal/load flag is set. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment) by timing retard. The Map A part only shapes how the estimate moves while conditions change: it is added through Filter A and taken off again through Filter B, so the settled value depends only on Map B x Retard Multiplier B.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) by timing retard. The Map A part only shapes how the estimate moves while conditions change: it is added through Filter A and taken off again through Filter B, so the settled value depends only on Map B x Retard Multiplier B.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (No Enrichment) by timing retard: more retard, hotter estimate.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched) by timing retard: more retard, hotter estimate.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Rising)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map A part of the estimate follows a rising value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Falling)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map A part of the estimate follows a falling value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Rising)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map B part of the estimate follows a rising value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Falling)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map B part of the estimate follows a falling value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Step
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred): an amount added to the estimate at the start of each fuel cut, by air quantity, which then decays away by Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Decay.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Decay
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred): how fast the fuel-cut term from Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Step decays, by air quantity (1.0 = no decay).

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor
table.description: On a hot restart, the A/F sensor exhaust model starts from the pipe temperature stored at engine stop, multiplied by this factor by how much the coolant has dropped since. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level: above light part throttle, above about 5200 rpm, or cold. Higher = earlier intake timing. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. This, not 1B, sets wide-open-throttle intake timing near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. This is the table that sets light-load intake timing on most cars.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to the final intake cam target near sea level (whatever the TGV state; with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to Intake Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor 3 so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Factor 3
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by coolant temperature on Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B, the cold-engine correction for the TGV-closed sea-level intake cam target.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more valve overlap. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Exhaust Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. Higher = more overlap. High-pedal meaning inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more overlap (internal EGR).

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target near sea level, scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. It applies whatever the TGV state: with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor 3. Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B is added on top of it in all TGV states, so with the TGVs closed both act.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor 3
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by coolant temperature on Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B, the cold-engine correction for the TGV-closed sea-level exhaust cam target.

table.name: AVCS Barometric Blend
table.description: Share (0-100 %) of the altitude (A) cam target tables versus the sea-level (B) tables, by barometric pressure.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is set, which is always the case with the manual coding (0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Descriptor 05C760. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set, on automatic/CVT cars.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear, which happens only with the AT/CVT coding (AT state FFF8A7DD 0 or 5; 0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Descriptor 05C754. Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay (TGV Closed)
table.description: TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay: time after start before the post-start idle air starts to decay. Its coolant input is inferred from the sibling table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Start Time (TGV Closed)
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air starts to rise, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air End Time (TGV Closed)
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air stops rising and starts to decay, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Level (TGV Closed)
table.description: Peak level of the staged post-start air, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Ramp Step (TGV Closed)
table.description: Rise of the staged post-start air every 40 ms between Start Time and End Time, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Decay (TGV Closed)
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms after End Time, by start type and coolant (smaller = faster fade). Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder
table.description: Correction by rpm and load added to EGR Upstream Pressure Estimate, scaled by EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder Multiplier.

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by barometric pressure on EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder.

table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum (Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Minimum coolant for TGV closing used only while a warm-up fallback flag is set.
TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Used while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set. Address 037A46. Confidence: read.

table.name: Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM
table.description:
Road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.
Same data block as descriptor 05D468 (one entry). Road speed per 1000 rpm for gear index 1-8. 0x11031C (read; called at seg_0x110000.c:1175 with cal 0x57585 bit 3, gear FFF8A8BA, speed FFF88BE8, selector FFF8A8C3): only when cal 0x57585 bit 3 is set, FFF8558A = this(gear) (the Alternate table when FFF8A8C3 = 2) and FFF85588 = speed x 28800 / FFF8558A -> FFF8B434. 0x110398 does the same with the second gear index FFF8A8BC (0x1143CC) through the shared descriptors -> FFF8B436. 0x116A0C (gear advice, gated by the same bit) uses B436/B434 as rpm x 0.1953125 to convert the current power to torque at those engine speeds (read). The values (11.3 to 53.9 km/h per 1000 rpm over 6 steps here, 11.0 to 53.9 over 8 in the Alternate table) do not fit the 6MT, so this belongs to another transmission (inferred). Descriptor 05D450. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM (Alternate)
table.description:
Alternate road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.
Details: When used: used instead of Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Same data block as descriptor 05D474 (one entry). 0x11031C (read; called at seg_0x110000.c:1175 with cal 0x57585 bit 3, gear FFF8A8BA, speed FFF88BE8, selector FFF8A8C3): only when cal 0x57585 bit 3 is set, FFF8558A = this(gear) (the Alternate table when FFF8A8C3 = 2) and FFF85588 = speed x 28800 / FFF8558A -> FFF8B434. 0x110398 does the same with the second gear index FFF8A8BC (0x1143CC) through the shared descriptors -> FFF8B436. 0x116A0C (gear advice, gated by the same bit) uses B436/B434 as rpm x 0.1953125 to convert the current power to torque at those engine speeds (read). The values (11.0 to 53.9 km/h per 1000 rpm over 8 steps here, 11.3 to 53.9 over 6 in the normal table) do not fit the 6MT, so this belongs to another transmission (inferred). Descriptor 05D45C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map
table.description:
Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies.
Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Descriptors 05D4D8, 05D504 and 05D518 share this data block (037352): 05D4D8 at the current torque FFF8B468 = DAM-blended torque FFF8B48A - FFF8A8CC x 128 (0x1161DC) and rpm, 05D504 / 05D518 at the torque needed for the same power in the lower / upper gear (read). One entry edits all three. Descriptor 05D4D8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Advice Downshift Maximum RPM (Alternate)
table.description:
Alternate rpm limit, by gear, below which a downshift may be advised by the gear advice function.
Details: When used: instead of 05D5B8 when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read): FFF85648 = this(lower gear FFF8A8BA); the lower gear is advised (FFF85679 = 1) only if its engine speed FFF8B434 <= FFF85648. 05D5B8 (normal) is 31232 = 6100 rpm for every gear. Descriptor 05D5C4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Advice Upshift Minimum RPM
table.description:
Minimum rpm in the next gear up, by pedal and gear, for an upshift to be advised by the gear advice function.
Details: When used: 05D5E4 replaces it when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read, lookup by pedal FFF88A5E and upper gear FFF8A8BC): FFF85646 = this; the upper gear is advised only if its engine speed FFF8B436 >= FFF85646. Descriptor 05D5D0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Advice Upshift Minimum RPM (Alternate)
table.description:
Alternate minimum rpm in the next gear up, by pedal and gear, for an upshift to be advised by the gear advice function.
Details: When used: instead of 05D5D0 when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read): FFF85646 = this(pedal FFF88A5E, upper gear FFF8A8BC); the upper gear is advised only if its engine speed FFF8B436 >= FFF85646. Descriptor 05D5E4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.description: How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1
table.description: Crankshaft roughness level, by rpm and load, that confirms channel 1 of the P219A A/F imbalance monitor. It sets no code by itself; P219A needs both this and A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1 exceeded. Raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never).

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2
table.description: Crankshaft roughness level that confirms channel 2 of the P219A monitor (paired with A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). Lower than Threshold 1, so more sensitive. Sets no code by itself; raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never).

table.name: (P000A) Intake Camshaft Position Slow Response (Bank 1)
table.description: Left cell, Enabled: 1 = this code can set and report, 0 = it never sets (its monitor still runs and other logic that reads the raw result may still react). Right cell, Fail-Safe: 1 = a failed test of this code raises the fail-safe request (what that request limits is not yet decoded). Needs RomRaider 1.0.0 or later.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT)

Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.
