table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
Intake Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level: above light part throttle, above about 5200 rpm, or cold. Higher = earlier intake timing. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
Intake Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. This, not 1B, sets wide-open-throttle intake timing near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. This is the table that sets light-load intake timing on most cars.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 2A (High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees, scaled by the intake coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees, scaled by the intake coolant factor) added to the TGV-closed target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to the final intake cam target near sea level (whatever the TGV state; with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 2B (High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees, scaled by the intake coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at sea level. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to Intake Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor 3 so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Intake Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Low, breakpoint 0x496BD)
table.description: Upper limit on the final intake cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Intake Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Mid, breakpoint 0x496BE)
table.description: Upper limit on the final intake cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Intake Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp High, breakpoint 0x496BC)
table.description: Upper limit on the final intake cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
Exhaust Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more valve overlap. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Exhaust Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
Exhaust Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. Higher = more overlap. High-pedal meaning inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more overlap (internal EGR).

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 2A (High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Extra exhaust cam retard (degrees, scaled by the exhaust coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Extra exhaust cam retard (degrees, scaled by the exhaust coolant factor) added to the TGV-closed target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target near sea level, scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. It applies whatever the TGV state: with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 2B (High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Extra exhaust cam retard (degrees, scaled by the exhaust coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at sea level. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor 3. Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B is added on top of it in all TGV states, so with the TGVs closed both act.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Low, breakpoint 0x496C5)
table.description: Upper limit on the final exhaust cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Mid, breakpoint 0x496C6)
table.description: Upper limit on the final exhaust cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp High, breakpoint 0x496C4)
table.description: Upper limit on the final exhaust cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: AVCS Barometric Blend
table.description: Share (0-100 %) of the altitude (A) cam target tables versus the sea-level (B) tables, by barometric pressure.

Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding. With the manual coding the idle mode never becomes 6 (0x0F2BCC passes the mode through unchanged while FFF88ADA bit 7 is set, and 0x0F354C produces only modes 1-5 and 7, read), so on a manual car edit Mode 5. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 6 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). Evidence: idle-speed reader 0x0FBC98 (= LF75404S 0x0F1BCC) calls the implicit-axis lookup on the same tables in the same order, and they sit in the same memory order (read): last lookup. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 7 is mapped to 8 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (read, 0x0F2BCC). Never on a manual car. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 8 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant for a cold-idle mode used when stopped below a coolant threshold.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 4 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is set, which is always the case with the manual coding (0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05C760 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00B50C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set, on automatic/CVT cars.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear, which happens only with the AT/CVT coding (AT state FFF8A7DD 0 or 5; 0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05C754 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00B500. Confidence: read.

Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 5 is mapped to 6 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (AT state code FFF8A7DD = 0 or 5, 0x0EC7A4; physical meaning not settled). Never on a manual car (read, 0x0F2BCC). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 5 is mapped to 6 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (AT state code FFF8A7DD = 0 or 5, 0x0EC7A4; physical meaning not settled). Never on a manual car (read, 0x0F2BCC). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4 with the TGVs commanded closed.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

TGV Coolant Minimum (Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Minimum coolant for TGV closing used only while a warm-up fallback flag is set.
TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Used while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 037A46 by the code that reads it (read). Address 040942. Confidence: read.

Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM
table.description:
Road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.
Same data block as descriptor 05D468 (one entry). Road speed per 1000 rpm for gear index 1-8. 0x11031C (read; called at seg_0x110000.c:1175 with cal 0x57585 bit 3, gear FFF8A8BA, speed FFF88BE8, selector FFF8A8C3): only when cal 0x57585 bit 3 is set, FFF8558A = this(gear) (the Alternate table when FFF8A8C3 = 2) and FFF85588 = speed x 28800 / FFF8558A -> FFF8B434. 0x110398 does the same with the second gear index FFF8A8BC (0x1143CC) through the shared descriptors -> FFF8B436. 0x116A0C (gear advice, gated by the same bit) uses B436/B434 as rpm x 0.1953125 to convert the current power to torque at those engine speeds (read). The values (11.3 to 53.9 km/h per 1000 rpm over 6 steps here, 11.0 to 53.9 over 8 in the Alternate table) do not fit the 6MT, so this belongs to another transmission (inferred). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D450 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C310. Confidence: inferred.

The values (11.0 to 53.9 km/h per 1000 rpm over 8 steps here, 11.3 to 53.9 over 6 in the normal table) do not fit the 6MT, so this belongs to another transmission (inferred). table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map
table.description:
Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies.
Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Descriptors 05D4D8, 05D504 and 05D518 share this data block (037352): 05D4D8 at the current torque FFF8B468 = DAM-blended torque FFF8B48A - FFF8A8CC x 128 (0x1161DC) and rpm, 05D504 / 05D518 at the torque needed for the same power in the lower / upper gear (read). One entry edits all three. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D4D8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C380. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Advice Downshift Maximum RPM (Alternate)
table.description:
Alternate rpm limit, by gear, below which a downshift may be advised by the gear advice function.
Details: When used: instead of 05D5B8 when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read): FFF85648 = this(lower gear FFF8A8BA); the lower gear is advised (FFF85679 = 1) only if its engine speed FFF8B434 <= FFF85648. 05D5B8 (normal) is 31232 = 6100 rpm for every gear. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D5C4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C46C. Confidence: inferred.

Details: When used: 05D5E4 replaces it when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read, lookup by pedal FFF88A5E and upper gear FFF8A8BC): FFF85646 = this; the upper gear is advised only if its engine speed FFF8B436 >= FFF85646. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D5D0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C478. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. Evidence: (from LF9C100P) Phase 11: the selector flag (2017 FFF8AD5A bit 0, 2018 FFF8BC16 bit 0, 2015 FFF8A7E2 bit 0) is state FFF8AD55 in {1,2,3,4,6} (0x103C64 / 0x0FD5FC in 2017). State 1 is forced while FFF889FB bit 7 (2015 FFF886AB bit 7) is set. the flag-clear table is for the other coding, whose state machine uses engine speed minus a received transmission speed (AT/CVT, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0E2BE4->0x0EDC08 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [1]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01C277 (1 reference(s), votes {'0227A7': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x0227A7 is accessed as u8. Matches the layout address. Confidence: read.

FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). Here 0x0E54DC reads 00A1DC (DAM 1) then 00A1C8 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6A; 0x0E5628 reads 00A1F0 (DAM 1) then 00A204 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6C (read). The consumers match by use: FFF8A73F / FFF8BB6A are used once (with FFF8A73B-type term), FFF8A741 / FFF8BB6C twice (x0x32 and with the FFF8A738-type term) (read). So 0x0E54DC = Alternate (0x0D9BD4) and 0x0E5628 = Blend B (0x0D9D48). Phase 18 had put the Alternate entries on the Blend B reader's tables (00A204/00A1F0), now shared with the Phase 19 Blend B entries (port_sanity duplicate). Confidence: read.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) for the manual car.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) 0x1110A0 is the counterpart of LF75404S 0x108BAC (same 4x4 lookup blocks, same counters FFF8xxxx run-time/re-entry logic, same clamp/select code; extended with new catalyst-heating terms after the blocks). caller seg_0x110000 line 1061; param_20=(FFF89E0D&1), param_14=(FFF8BC16&1); function body identical to LF79002P 0x117018 after address normalisation (0 differing lines). group 1, param_20!=0 branch, lookup 1 -> &DAT_00BE08 (LF75404S 05D01C). ROM: 00BE08 16x16 s8 data s8@032CAC; axes identical to LF75404S. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor)

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description: Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred).

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 5 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 5 (warm idle) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 6 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 7 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 7 (warm-up drive-off) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 7 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 7 (warm-up drive-off) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 7)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)

The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0E2BE4->0x0EDC08 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [1]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01C277 (1 reference(s), votes {'0227A7': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x0227A7 is accessed as u8. Matches the layout address. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) timing parent 0x0EA868 calls the two code-identical 77-insn DAM blend readers as callees 21 and 22 (0x8A0 calls not counted), as LF75404S 0x0DF0B8 calls 0x0D9BD4 (Alternate: 05B560 DAM 1, then 05B54C DAM 0, output FFF8A73F) and 0x0D9D48 (Blend B: 05B574 DAM 1, then 05B588 DAM 0, output FFF8A741) as callees 20 and 21 (read). Here 0x0E54DC reads 00A1DC (DAM 1) then 00A1C8 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6A; 0x0E5628 reads 00A1F0 (DAM 1) then 00A204 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6C (read). The consumers match by use: FFF8A73F / FFF8BB6A are used once (with FFF8A73B-type term), FFF8A741 / FFF8BB6C twice (x0x32 and with the FFF8A738-type term) (read). So 0x0E54DC = Alternate (0x0D9BD4) and 0x0E5628 = Blend B (0x0D9D48). Phase 18 had put the Alternate entries on the Blend B reader's tables (00A204/00A1F0), now shared with the Phase 19 Blend B entries (port_sanity duplicate). Confidence: read.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) for the manual car.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) 0x1110A0 is the counterpart of LF75404S 0x108BAC (same 4x4 lookup blocks, same counters FFF8xxxx run-time/re-entry logic, same clamp/select code; extended with new catalyst-heating terms after the blocks). caller seg_0x110000 line 1061; param_20=(FFF89E0D&1), param_14=(FFF8BC16&1); function body identical to LF79002P 0x117018 after address normalisation (0 differing lines). group 1, param_20!=0 branch, lookup 1 -> &DAT_00BE08 (LF75404S 05D01C). ROM: 00BE08 16x16 s8 data s8@032CAC; axes identical to LF75404S. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1) for the manual car.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) 0x1110A0 is the counterpart of LF75404S 0x108BAC (same 4x4 lookup blocks, same counters FFF8xxxx run-time/re-entry logic, same clamp/select code; extended with new catalyst-heating terms after the blocks). caller seg_0x110000 line 1061; param_20=(FFF89E0D&1), param_14=(FFF8BC16&1); function body identical to LF79002P 0x117018 after address normalisation (0 differing lines). group 1, param_20!=0, lookup 4 -> &DAT_00BF44 (LF75404S 05D134). ROM: 00BF44 16x16 s8 data s8@032FCC; axes identical to LF75404S. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description: Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 2: SI-Drive Sport (S). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT, Monitor)

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description: Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred).

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 5 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 5 (warm idle) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 6 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 7 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 7 (warm-up drive-off) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 7 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 7 (warm-up drive-off) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 7)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, Coolant)
table.description: Idle air taken away, by coolant, while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive (pedal released, slow) to offset the load of the transmission. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, RPM Error)
table.description: Correction to Idle Air Reduction In Drive by rpm error (actual minus target) and coolant, for automatic/CVT cars idling in Drive. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward (AT/CVT, State 0/5)
table.description: Automatic/CVT version of Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward, used in two transmission states only: extra or less idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear, AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as stopped in gear for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral, AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as in neutral/park for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Maximum
table.description: Upper limit, by barometric pressure, of a modelled brake-booster vacuum.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Manifold Threshold
table.description: Manifold-vacuum threshold, by barometric pressure, for a brake-booster vacuum model.

table.name: Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM
table.description: Road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.

table.name: Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.

table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map
table.description: Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies.

table.name: Gear Advice Downshift Maximum RPM (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate rpm limit, by gear, below which a downshift may be advised by the gear advice function.

table.name: Gear Advice Upshift Minimum RPM
table.description: Minimum rpm in the next gear up, by pedal and gear, for an upshift to be advised by the gear advice function.

table.name: Gear Advice Upshift Minimum RPM (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate minimum rpm in the next gear up, by pedal and gear, for an upshift to be advised by the gear advice function.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. Evidence: (from LF9C100P) Phase 11: the selector flag (2017 FFF8AD5A bit 0, 2018 FFF8BC16 bit 0, 2015 FFF8A7E2 bit 0) is state FFF8AD55 in {1,2,3,4,6} (0x103C64 / 0x0FD5FC in 2017). State 1 is forced while FFF889FB bit 7 (2015 FFF886AB bit 7) is set. the flag-clear table is for the other coding, whose state machine uses engine speed minus a received transmission speed (AT/CVT, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback).
Details: When used: Only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding (Cal Switches: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT); unused on a manual car (read). LF9C000C: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) Phase 11: the selector flag (2017 FFF8AD5A bit 0, 2018 FFF8BC16 bit 0, 2015 FFF8A7E2 bit 0) is state FFF8AD55 in {1,2,3,4,6} (0x103C64 / 0x0FD5FC in 2017). State 1 is forced while FFF889FB bit 7 (2015 FFF886AB bit 7) is set. the flag-clear table is for the other coding, whose state machine uses engine speed minus a received transmission speed (AT/CVT, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0E2BE4->0x0EDC08 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [1]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01C277 (1 reference(s), votes {'0227A7': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x0227A7 is accessed as u8. Matches the layout address. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 6)

Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 6. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0E2BE4->0x0EDC08 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [1]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01C276 (1 reference(s), votes {'0227A6': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x0227A6 is accessed as u8. Matches the layout address. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) timing parent 0x0EA868 calls the two code-identical 77-insn DAM blend readers as callees 21 and 22 (0x8A0 calls not counted), as LF75404S 0x0DF0B8 calls 0x0D9BD4 (Alternate: 05B560 DAM 1, then 05B54C DAM 0, output FFF8A73F) and 0x0D9D48 (Blend B: 05B574 DAM 1, then 05B588 DAM 0, output FFF8A741) as callees 20 and 21 (read). Here 0x0E54DC reads 00A1DC (DAM 1) then 00A1C8 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6A; 0x0E5628 reads 00A1F0 (DAM 1) then 00A204 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6C (read). The consumers match by use: FFF8A73F / FFF8BB6A are used once (with FFF8A73B-type term), FFF8A741 / FFF8BB6C twice (x0x32 and with the FFF8A738-type term) (read). So 0x0E54DC = Alternate (0x0D9BD4) and 0x0E5628 = Blend B (0x0D9D48). Phase 18 had put the Alternate entries on the Blend B reader's tables (00A204/00A1F0), now shared with the Phase 19 Blend B entries (port_sanity duplicate). Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 1)
table.description:

FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) timing parent 0x0EA868 calls the two code-identical 77-insn DAM blend readers as callees 21 and 22 (0x8A0 calls not counted), as LF75404S 0x0DF0B8 calls 0x0D9BD4 (Alternate: 05B560 DAM 1, then 05B54C DAM 0, output FFF8A73F) and 0x0D9D48 (Blend B: 05B574 DAM 1, then 05B588 DAM 0, output FFF8A741) as callees 20 and 21 (read). Here 0x0E54DC reads 00A1DC (DAM 1) then 00A1C8 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6A; 0x0E5628 reads 00A1F0 (DAM 1) then 00A204 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6C (read). The consumers match by use: FFF8A73F / FFF8BB6A are used once (with FFF8A73B-type term), FFF8A741 / FFF8BB6C twice (x0x32 and with the FFF8A738-type term) (read). So 0x0E54DC = Alternate (0x0D9BD4) and 0x0E5628 = Blend B (0x0D9D48). Phase 18 had put the Alternate entries on the Blend B reader's tables (00A204/00A1F0), now shared with the Phase 19 Blend B entries (port_sanity duplicate). Confidence: read.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) for the manual car.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) 0x1110A0 is the counterpart of LF75404S 0x108BAC (same 4x4 lookup blocks, same counters FFF8xxxx run-time/re-entry logic, same clamp/select code; extended with new catalyst-heating terms after the blocks). caller seg_0x110000 line 1061; param_20=(FFF89E0D&1), param_14=(FFF8BC16&1); function body identical to LF79002P 0x117018 after address normalisation (0 differing lines). group 1, param_20!=0 branch, lookup 1 -> &DAT_00BE08 (LF75404S 05D01C). ROM: 00BE08 16x16 s8 data s8@032CAC; axes identical to LF75404S. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).

table.description: Fuel removed from the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its own DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). Leaning only works where Primary Open Loop Fueling is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier
Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 066D98. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group plus its knock additive, used only with the 'Use Alternate Map' calibration switch set.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x2F79A bit 4 set and DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x1391C (16). Replaces the TGV/AVCS blend plus knock additive in FFF8A681. 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear. With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05AC00 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 066B38. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05A804 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0666DC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description:
Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.
Details: When used: see Additional Enrichment A: B applies when coolant < cal 0x13E1A or rpm >= cal 0x13E0C (A when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E; in between the last value is held), and the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1. Second source table of FFF8AFE8. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05A818 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0666F0. Confidence: inferred.

Injection Timing (Double Injection, 1st)
table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, Monitor)
Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor)
Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT, Monitor)
Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Drive mode 3: SI-Drive Intelligent (I). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.
Details: When used: whenever FFF88ADA bit 7 (manual-transmission coding) is clear, i.e. on the AT/CVT coding. The A/B weight FFF8AE26 (0x0B9C78) starts at 0 and its step cals 0x22FBE/0x22FC0 are 0, so it stays 0 and the output is this table alone; the matching non-AT/CVT table is then ignored (read). FFF88ADA bit 7 is set on the manual coding, so this table is unused on manual cars. Driver-requested torque from rpm and pedal (0x0BB588, read): FFF8AEB0 = A x FFF8AE26/32768 + B x (1 - FFF8AE26/32768), torque above the zero point, into FFF8AEB0; FFF8AE26 ramps between 0 and 32768 under a condition (0x0B9C78). Table B of map set 1 = Drive Mode 3 (0x0BDBD8 combines the four sets by the drive-mode byte FFF8A8C1 and per-mode scale cals 0x1FAFE-0x1FB00; SI-Drive positions: mode 4 = Sport Sharp, mode 2 = Sport, mode 3 = Intelligent (least torque for a given pedal in both images), mode 1 = the default used when no valid SI-Drive request is received, and the only set on cars without SI-Drive). KEEP Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT, Monitor) identical (inferred safety copy). Evidence: port from LF79002P (call-site mapping on near-identical code); the LF75404S-based pick 06530C is the known sibling crosswise pairing seen in LF79002P/LF9C100P (read: confirmed by the decompiled callers / reader positions against LF79002P, 2026-10-29). Confidence: inferred.
